review_scope: Fresh manual review of the eight listed candidate PNGs against the retained user contract, reference scope, handoff text, and static prototype declarations. No independent reference image is provided for this supplemental batch. This is a batch-level visual finding, not a clean-round conclusion.

evidence_binding.hash_method: PowerShell Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 on each current candidate PNG
evidence_binding.case_metadata_reviewed: The salient application state, capture metadata, recorded checks, intentional differences, and processed-artwork geometry were read for every case. The recorded checks report no failures; they were not rerun.

observations: The portrait library visibly contains one imported Chapter 1 item, with an unread badge and a downloaded icon beside its title. This agrees with the recorded library_count of 1 and the local imported book identity.

The continuation card displays the imported cover, Chapter 1, a 1/3 position, a progress track, and a distinct arrow action. The adjacent daily-update card shows an empty update state without clipping either card.

The selected library tab, single occupied grid position, centered 1/1 folio, and five-item bottom navigation remain legible and separate. The large unused grid area is consistent with a one-book library rather than missing rendered entries.
The saved notification is a white outlined status box above the folio on this non-reader route. No shadow, dimmed backdrop, overlapping label, or unexplained blank content region is visible.

The final page visibly contains its outlined page frame, large black content rectangle, and printed OFFLINE PAGE 10 label. No separate app header, status bar, bookmark ribbon, footer, notification, or reader panel is visible.

The sole content image occupies the portrait scene without an empty second-page slot or decorative center seam. The recorded final position is 3/3, with effective spread disabled and second_path null, so the portrait single-page presentation agrees with the actual native state despite the case name.

The recorded processed-image size is 1814 by 2480, fitted into the complete 930 by 1240 viewport at destination [12, 0, 919, 1240]. The narrow outer white strips and the artwork's own white area are consistent with that aspect fit and do not establish an application viewport inset.

The case records an actual odd-length local chapter ending with one full-viewport image. The visible capture supports that final scene; the artwork-only pixel oracle is supporting metadata rather than a substitute for this manual inspection.

The capture shows the normal portrait manga-detail route after leaving the reader: top status and back controls, a left information column, and a separate chapter directory. No reader overlay or landscape shell remains visible.

The left column contains the cover, title, author, metadata, 12/40 continuation position, three actions, description, and tags without clipped text. Its narrower information allocation agrees with the prototype's 384-pixel sidebar rather than equal-width halves.

The right directory displays sixteen readable chapter rows, numbered 86 through 71, with dates and download controls. The 1/6 folio and next-page action remain clear at the bottom, and no main dock is present on the detail route.

The case's launch screen is reader, but the captured route and application state are detail with display_landscape false. The visible portrait detail page is consistent with that returned state; the launch-screen label is not treated as the final route.

The image contains comic artwork only: a wide skyline panel above a dotted panel, a radial-line panel, and a tall crosshatched panel. The patterns belong to the artwork and are not a stippled modal backdrop.

The upper-right corner, top edge, center seam area, and bottom edge show no remaining menu strip, bookmark ribbon, status bar, footer label, notification, sheet outline, or dimming after panel closure.
The recorded state identifies page 12/40 with menu false, an empty reader_panel, a ready image, and no inflight reader work. The observed pure artwork scene agrees with those state values.
The 24-pixel side fit at destination [24, 0, 906, 1240] follows the recorded 1764 by 2480 processed image. These white side areas are not evidence of reserved application chrome.

The checkpoint capture was individually viewed. It shows the skyline, dotted, radial, and crosshatched artwork panels without an app status bar, menu, bookmark ribbon, progress footer, notification, or blank replacement frame.

The recorded checkpoint is page 20/40, zoom 1, offset 0, and a closed menu. The artwork extends across the complete portrait fit region with the same narrow aspect-fit side areas as the panel-close scene.

Its PNG hash matches the restored capture, supporting a visually unchanged checkpoint scene. The same artwork also appears in the panel-close case at a different recorded page; therefore the screenshot alone does not establish the numeric page identity or checkpoint persistence.

The restored capture was separately opened and inspected. Its skyline, dotted, radial, and crosshatched artwork is visually unchanged from the checkpoint, including the portrait aspect fit and absence of app chrome.
No library page, startup frame, loading placeholder, recovery panel, saved notification, footer, or reader menu remains visible in the restored scene.

Although the process launch screen is library, the captured application route is reader at page 20/40, zoom 1, offset 0, with a closed menu and ready image. Those values agree with the checkpoint metadata, and the original PNG hashes also agree.

The existing case records a fresh --resume process restoring every artwork pixel. This review supports the visible restored result only; it does not independently replay persistence or establish physical sleep and wake behavior.

The post-input image visibly contains a tall radial-line panel on the left, two dotted panels on the right, and a lower vertical-line panel with a speech balloon. No menu, tap-zone guide, footer, notification, or bookmark ribbon overlays the artwork.

The current state identifies page 11/40 with reading_direction rtl and tap_layout reversed. The displayed reader session agrees with page 11 and remains portrait, with no second image or pending reader work.

The content remains continuous through the full portrait fit region. Its side white areas and content touching the top and bottom agree with the recorded processed-image fit rather than demonstrating a reader inset or missing UI repaint.

The result screenshot cannot show which physical region was tapped or prove the reversed mapping. The final image is also shared by the RTL-input case, so numerical page movement is supported by metadata rather than by a unique page inscription.

This candidate was individually viewed despite sharing an image hash with the reversed-input case. The radial, dotted, and vertical-line comic panels show no residual reader tools, status bar, page label, bookmark ribbon, notification, or visible tap-zone decoration.

The bound state identifies page 13/40, reading_direction rtl, tap_layout thirds, menu false, and a ready single image. The actual route is reader and the image remains in the expected portrait viewport.

There is no unexpected blank paired-page slot, center gutter decoration, or panel remnant. The recorded 1764 by 2480 processed image is fitted to destination [24, 0, 906, 1240], explaining the narrow side white areas.

The screenshot establishes a clean visible end state. It cannot independently establish right-to-left input ordering or the page-number transition because the artwork is repeated and app progress labels are intentionally absent in the closed reader.

coverage_gaps: The batch supplies no independent reference PNG. Visual review uses the retained scope and static handoff/prototype declarations and does not claim a pixel comparison against an unseen reference.

All six reader captures show closed-menu end states. This batch does not cover the default menu-open layout, visible unavailable software controls, capability-dependent hardware controls, or content-dependent open-sheet height.

Static screenshots do not prove invisible footer-cycle hit-zone removal, menu-open input suppression, outside-dismiss behavior, reversed tap mapping, RTL event ordering, or the cover-alone policy across landscape spread boundaries. Existing case metadata is supporting evidence, not an independently replayed interaction.

Repeated artwork and identical PNGs across different recorded page numbers prevent visual identification of the exact numerical page in several reader cases. Checkpoint and restored images visibly agree, while persistence and page identity depend on the bound state and prior recorded checks.
Desktop captures do not establish physical Kindle wake behavior, rotation sensors, e-ink refresh waveforms, hardware controls, pen support, or a 512 MiB memory qualification.
limitations: Each of the eight listed original candidate PNGs was actually opened with tools.view_image. No other PNG, reference image, expected oracle image, or difference image was loaded.

Current PNG hashes were read directly with Get-FileHash and matched both the input manifest and each case's screenshot evidence. All cases identify run a1baf3fe3dc2 and the specified binary and source hashes.
The existing zero-difference artwork-oracle results were read only as supporting metadata. They do not replace manual review and cannot establish invisible interaction behavior.

Actual artwork, aspect-fit white areas, record counts, titles, progress values, and times were not treated as defects merely because they differ from reference sample data. The closed-reader ribbon and footer omissions follow the explicit user override.

Only existing PNGs and text/JSON evidence were read, candidate hashes were computed, and this review JSON was written. No application, prototype runtime, build, test suite, runtime probe, Git operation, or product modification was performed.
No definite visible issue was found in this eight-case batch. This statement does not assert completion of the full review round or qualify a clean-round streak.
